chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman and Jamil ibn Darradj, from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him saying: 'The grandfather shares equally with the brothers, regardless of how many there are, even if they are one hundred thousand.'

key_terms.مَا بَلَغُوا: As many as they are / regardless of the number

ai.seo_question: Does the grandfather inherit equally with the brothers regardless of their number?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of 'al-jadd yuqasimu al-ikhwah' (the grandfather shares with the brothers), establishing that the paternal grandfather is treated as a sibling in inheritance distribution rather than a primary ancestor who excludes others. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for resolving conflicts between the 'Hajb' (exclusion) and 'Qasamah' (sharing) rules, ensuring the grandfather receives an equal portion regardless of the quantity of full brothers present. It underscores the egalitarian nature of the grandfather's share within the 'Asabah' (residuary) category when competing with direct male descendants of the same degree.
